asr_text: The research team suggests that a thick layer of rock full of gaps may have worked like insulation. Just as insulation in a house keeps heat from escaping, this layer may have made it harder for heat inside the moon to escape. As a result, the moon may have cooled and shrunk more slowly. In other words, the moon may have kept warm in its rock coat, but it is too soon to end the mystery by saying the coat is the culprit. For now, it is just one possible explanation for the difference. Counting cliffs on the moon led to its inner heat, and then to the coat's warmth. Not how it feels to wear, but how well it keeps heat in. The wrinkles were an important clue to how the moon cooled. Next time you look up at the moon, imagine the rock coat beneath its round shape, too. The moon's way of dressing has more to it than meets the eye.

page_script_text: The research team suggests that a thick layer of rock full of gaps may have worked like insulation. Just as insulation in a house keeps heat from escaping, this layer may have made it harder for heat inside the Moon to escape. As a result, the Moon may have cooled and shrunk more slowly. In other words, the Moon may have kept warm in its rock coat. But it is too soon to end the mystery by saying, “The coat is the culprit!” For now, it is just one possible explanation for the difference. Counting cliffs on the Moon led to its inner heat, and then to the coat’s warmth—not how it feels to wear, but how well it keeps heat in. The wrinkles were an important clue to how the Moon cooled. Next time you look up at the Moon, imagine the “rock coat” beneath its round shape, too. The Moon’s way of dressing has more to it than meets the eye.
